details: This package is a dependency-confusion proof of concept. Its postinstall hook (node beacon.cjs) — and its index.js entry point, which calls the same beacon on import — sends a single JSON POST of install metadata to hxxp://185[.]158[.]107[.]175:8787/_ah/dc with an X-Beacon-Package header. The reported fields are limited to the package name, hostname, install path (__dirname), working directory, and the npm user the publisher string. It reads no environment variables, credentials, tokens, or files, spawns no processes, and loads no second stage; index.js exports a no-op Proxy shim so imports do not fail. The README describes the package as published for an authorized dependency-confusion test that only reports that it was installed. This package is a dependency-confusion proof of concept. Its package.json declares a postinstall hook that runs beacon.cjs, and index.js also invokes the same beacon when the module is required, so an install or an import both trigger a callback. The beacon sends an HTTP POST to hxxp://185[.]158[.]107[.]175:8787/_ah/dc with a JSON body containing only install metadata — the package name, the machine hostname, the install directory, the working directory and the npm/node user agent — plus an x-beacon-package header naming the package. The package ships a no-op Proxy shim so that a build importing the real package name completes instead of crashing, and its README states it was published as an authorized dependency-confusion test that reports only that it was installed. No credentials, environment values, tokens, wallet data or file contents are read or transmitted.
